text:
maria: Ran a perfetto trace during the nightly decode job. Seeing attention stalls once seq_len > 2048, filing the trace here: https://perfetto.local/trace/abc123 (internal).
cheng: link works, thanks. quick q — was this on the dedicated cluster or local rig?
maria: dedicated-gpu-3, driver 525, cuda 12.1. workload: chat model v2, warm KV cache for most users.
ryan: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet you saw? quick glance helps.
maria: pasted the timeline from perfetto (simplified):
```
0. dec_loop (2.1ms)
1. flash_attn_fwd_fast (0.9ms)
2. cudaMemcpyAsync (kv_read) (5.8ms)
3. fused_attn_v2 (12.4ms)
4. kv_cache_write (2.2ms)
5. post_process (0.4ms)
```
maria: note the fused_attn_v2 run is much slower than flash_attn_fwd_fast for the same step when seq_len goes up.
cheng: that cudaMemcpyAsync for kv_read is huge. are we pulling KV from host memory every token?
maria: seems like it — older deploy used host RAM + pinned copies for big caches. the new mempool change didn't pin pages for some sizes.
ryan: that would explain the stall. memcpy over PCIe per token kills latency. we should prefetch KV pages to GPU or keep them resident when model pinned.
kai: also check batching heuristics. If batching window is too small we'll get many tiny batches causing repeated memcpy rampups.
yan: agree. what's current batcher window for decode? 2ms? sounds like we tuned for latency but now cost is throughput regress.
maria: current config: dynamic window: min 1ms, max 5ms, flush on n=8. With seq_len growing the kernel cost dominates but we create many small GPU transfers.
cheng: proposed quick fixes:
- kernel selector: prefer flash_attn variants for mid-long seqs up to 4096 if memory layout matches
- prefetch KV to GPU for hot sessions (background async memcpy)
- change batching to prefer size-based aggregation: expand window to 8ms when seq_avg > 1024
- add a pinned-mempool fallback if page not pinned

kai: sounds good. one more: fuse vs flash — fused_attn_v2 is doing an extra reorder for kv-layout that costs O(N^2) for long seqs; maybe choose flash which is memory-optimized.
maria: here's a quick nvprof-like kernel list from a follow-up run (nvprof summary):
```
GPU time: 36.8ms
flash_attn_fwd_fast: 6.7ms (18%)
fused_attn_v2: 17.9ms (49%)
kv_cache_read: 8.3ms (22%)
memcpy_h2d_async: 3.9ms (11%)
```
ryan: fused_attn_v2 49% is rough. we should try a variant switch in the selector based on seq_len and batch_size. Also track temp memory and kernel workspace size — fused might allocate a lot causing fragmentation.
cheng: action items:
- cheng: add perfetto trace marker hooks around KV read/write (so we can correlate memcpy slices) — ETA tomorrow
- ryan: prototype background prefetch (cudaMemcpyAsync stream with events) and run A/B for a handful of sessions — ETA 2 days
- kai: implement kernel selector rule: if seq_len > 1024 and batch_size >= 4 -> prefer flash_attn_fwd_fast, else fused_attn_v2 as fallback. include ability to force via env var — ETA 3 days
- maria: roll a canary with pinned mempool fallback on dedicated-gpu-3 and collect perfetto traces — ETA tomorrow afternoon
perf-bot: scheduled perfetto capture job on dedicated-gpu-3 at 18:00 UTC
maria: also noticed a perf regression around commit c4d9a1 -> added a test case to reproduce locally.
ryan: good. after changes please add a microbenchmark (seq sweep 128..8192) to the perf repo so CI catches regressions.
cheng: will add perfetto link to the regression ticket and tag the infra team.
maria: thanks all. tagging @kai and @ryan to review the selector patch before merge. :thumbsup:
kai: ack, will PR early tomorrow. :eyes:
maria: closing thread, will post updated traces once the preftech/prototype is in.
